subject.title: openclaw models fallbacks {list,add,remove,clear} ignores --agent, always operates on agents.defaults.model.fallbacks

question: Should `models fallbacks --agent` become a supported per-agent text fallback editor while `image-fallbacks --agent` is rejected, or should all fallback commands reject inherited agent scope and remain defaults-only?
rationale: Current source supports per-agent text fallbacks but the documented CLI contract is global, and no equivalent per-agent image fallback configuration exists; source inspection cannot safely choose that public CLI contract.

options.title: Support Text Agent Scope
options.body: Make text fallback commands create or update explicit per-agent overrides, and reject agent scope for image fallbacks until that schema exists.

options.title: Keep Defaults Only
options.body: Reject `--agent` consistently for all fallback commands and retain the currently documented global-only behavior.

options.title: Expand Both Contracts
options.body: Add per-agent text and image fallback configuration plus CLI support, accepting a broader schema and compatibility change.

recommendation.title: Support Text Agent Scope
recommendation.body: Make text fallback commands create or update explicit per-agent overrides, and reject agent scope for image fallbacks until that schema exists.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged per-agent fallback work defines the closest existing ownership and inheritance semantics for this decision.
